source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

26073.t:
Isabella County swung toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race, flipping from Trump to El-Sayed. Trump carried it by 8 points in 2024; El-Sayed leads Rogers here by 3, 13,149 votes to 12,339. That 11-point move is the third-largest of Michigan's 83 counties, all of which moved left. It outpaced the state's 9-point shift and the typical Michigan county's 6, though not the typical 14-point move nationally. Similar Michigan counties shifted less: Clinton and Berrien by 6 points each, Emmet by about 5. All three stayed Republican.

About 26,057 votes have been cast so far, 85% of the 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 92% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

26061.t:

Mike Rogers beat Abdul El-Sayed here by 8 points, 8,711 votes to 7,396, after Donald Trump carried it by 17 points in 2024. That is a 9-point move toward the Democrats, a little more than Michigan's statewide swing of 9 points (rounded from 8.5). It ranks ninth among the state's 83 counties, all of which moved left, and beats the typical Michigan county's 6 points. It falls short of the national typical move of 14.

Similar counties moved less, with Charlevoix and Manistee each shifting 5 points, except Gogebic, which matched Houghton at 9. Turnout was 85% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.
